facts.text: Stillwater earned its name when a pioneer named Payne walked up to Stillwater Creek and declared the town should be called Still Water.
Washington Irving first described the area in 1832, noting the prairie landscape that would later become Stillwater’s backdrop.
The first train arrived in 1900, marking Stillwater’s entry into the railroad era and spurring rapid growth.
The Sheerar Museum of Stillwater History preserves artifacts that chronicle the city’s journey from a frontier settlement to a college town.
Stillwater hosts the National Wrestling Hall of Fame & Museum, celebrating the sport’s heritage and local wrestling legends.
Every May, the Oklahoma Special Olympics’ Annual Summer Games bring athletes and families to Stillwater for a month of competition and community.
